The Montreal YMCA 
The Montreal YMCA Foundation Inc. 


Chairman’s 
Report 


The year which is coming to a close 
has been extremely eventful, both on 
a local and international level. In fact, 
we witnessed some very positive 
events, such as the dismantling of 
the Berlin Wall, and others which 
were not so uplifting, such as the Oka 
Crisis and war in the Persian Gulf. 
Usually, it is under such circumstances 
that the YMCA succeeds in distin- 
guishing itself. Once again, history 
repeated itself. 


This year, the Montreal YMCA, more 
than ever before, played a role of 
social entrepreneur within several 
Montreal communities. Indeed, today 
the Association is recognized as a 
leader in several fields such as urban 
development, employability training, 
community justice initiatives and the 
rights of ethnic minorities. As a 
result, when traditional institutions, 
because of a lack of resources, are 
unable to respond to specific needs, 
often it is towards the YMCA that 
they turn for help. 


A new challenge marked the end of 
this fiscal year: that of searching for a 
new Director General. Our current 
Director, Sol Kasimer, my long time 
partner and friend, will soon become 
Director General of YMCA Canada, in 
Toronto. Consequently, we must 
choose a successor who will be able 
to continue to lead the YMCA in the 
positive direction it has taken. 


In closing, | wish to express my 
heartfelt thanks to the employees 
and volunteers of the Montreal / 
Association, without whom we could 
not respond so effectively to the // 
needs of Montrealers. Also, | wish / 
to take this opportunity to spectfically 


thank my partner, Sol Kasimer,’ for 
his perspective and commitment 

and wish him every success with 
his new challenge. iy NG : 


CALF 


Claude Lemay 
Chairman of the Board

Director General’s 
Report 


Although extremely stimulating, 
1990-91 was indeed a difficult year. 
Difficult because of the current eco- 
nomic situation, which had its effect 
on us, as well as all Canadians. But 
stimulating because, once again 
despite everything, we succeeded 
in responding to the needs of the 
Montreal community. In fact, even 
during this economic recession, our 
centres remained accessible to all 
citizens, regardless of their economic 
situation. 


This fiscal year was also stimulating 
on another level. In fact, now that 
the Montreal YMCA has completed 
its second strategic planning study 
and chosen the direction it wants to 
take, it is more than ever before 
ready to expand into other franco- 
phone communities, like Montreal 
East, Laval and the South Shore. 

At the moment, a team composed 

of volunteers and staff members is 
examining the possibility of extending 
Our programs and services to a greater 
number of Montrealers. | am con- 
vinced that, no matter where we 
decide to establish new YMCA facil- 
ities, we will continue our tradition of 
SUCCeSS. 


Finally, both on a professional and 
personal level, this fiscal year marks 
the end of a profoundly stimulating 


11-year period for me. Indeed, after, iy 


y 


serious reflection, | have agreed to / 4 i 


take on the responsibility of Director 


General of YMCA Canada, in Toronto: Ae 


It is difficult to leave the Montreal Y 


am leaving with full confidence that,“ 
the Montreal YMCA is in good hands 
because of you, volunteers and staff 


after so many challenging years, but |

a heartfelt thanks to each and every\, \.

Montreal YMCA 


A Social 
Entrepreneur 


For 1990-91, the Montreal YMCA 
chose to concentrate on its role as 
social entrepreneur within the 
Montreal community. In doing so, 

it distinguished itself in four specific 
areas of intervention namely, employ- 
ability training, the rights of ethnic 
minorities, urban development and 
community justice initiatives. 


Urban 
Development 


During the course of the past few 
years, the situation of both the 
homeless and itinerant population in 
Montreal has become alarming. What 
was previously considered a problem 
which affected a certain age group is 
now, as we can all see today, affect- 
ing a steadily increasing number of 


i young people who have no permanent 


housing and are literally living on the 
street. 


Through its Downtown branch, the 
Montreal YMCA is striving to solve 
this problem by continuing to support 
the activities of the Fédération des 
O.S.B.L. d'habitation de Montréal 
(FOHM), a coalition of 18 rooming 
houses which are slated for Montreal's 
itinerant population. Notably, this 
year FOHM held a major news 
conference in order to sensitize the 
Montreal community to the problem 
of itinerancy and to make it aware of 
its solution, a solution that advocates 
social housing which is supported by 
the community. Following this press 
conference, as chairperson of FOHM, 
Francoise Fréchette, Director of 
Community Development for the 
Downtown YMCA, received the 
Woman of the Year award in the 
“Social and Humanitarian Action" 
category. 


Through its long-term commitment to 
community organizations, more than 
ever before, the Montreal YMCA 
favors solutions which are adapted to 
the needs of the itinerant population 
of Montreal. 


The Rights of Ethnic 
Minorities 


Through the initiative of its head 
office and thanks to a Secretary of 
State grant, the Montreal YMCA 
created an innovative program known 
as Minority Achievement Program. 


The Minority Achievement Program, 
whose goal is to help students from 
visible minorities set educational and 
professional goals for themselves and 
achieve these, is a partnership estab- 
lished between visible minorities and 
the business world. This program 
works hard at finding summer 
employment for students who are 
members of these communities by 
setting up a network of potential 
employers. To date, various corpo- 
rations, such as the M.U.C.T.C., 

the Royal Bank of Canada and la 
Fédération des caisses populaires 
Desjardins, have promised to support 
the Program. Moreover, a steering 
committee has been organized, and 
it is only a matter of time before the 
first participants join the Program. 


Employability 
Training 


Once again, this year, two Montreal 
YMCA projects, the Job Generation 
program and Enterprise Centre, clearly 
exemplified the YMCA's commitment 
to the issue of employability training. 


Already in its tenth year of operations, 
the Job Generation program continued 
to develop and find new solutions 

to unemployment among young 
Montrealers who are from ethnic 
origins. 


The Program, whose operations are 
now located on avenue Du Parc, 
achieved tremendous success during 
this last fiscal year. In fact, between 
75% and 80% of participants in the 
Program succeeded in finding work or 
réturned to school, and 95% of partic- 
ipants said that they were quite satis- 
fied with the training they received. 


As far as the Enterprise Centre is 
concerned, it should be noted that 
since its creation, four years ago, this 
business incubator helped start up a 
hundred or so new businesses which 
generated investments exceeding the 
$3,500,000 mark. 


More than ever before, the Centre is 
intent on demonstrating that the 
spirit of entrepreneurship is flourish- 
ing in the Montreal community. Who 
knows if the Armand Bombardiers 
and Louis-Alphonse Desjardins's of 
tomorrow are not in the process of 
acquiring skills which will help them 
become prosperous entrepreneurs! 


A counselling session 
within the context of the 
Job Generation Program. 


Three young participants 
in the Diversion Program 
of the West Island YMCA 
Community Centre. 


Community Justice 
Initiatives 


In reality, the Montreal YMCA is "the 
pioneer" in the field of community 
justice initiatives. As a matter of fact, 
for some thirty years now, the Asso- 
ciation has been working with youth 
and young adults who have difficulty 
with the law or are prone to run into 
trouble with the law. 


During the past year, the West Island 
YMCA Community Centre, recognized 
for its excellent programs for youth 
who are in difficulty, focused on initia- 
tives aimed at prevention. Among 
these should be noted the "! Do Have 
Choices program, which aims at pre- 
venting high-school students from 
dropping out; the PARADE program, 
which sensitizes youth and parents to 
the ill effects of alcohol and drugs; 
the YMCA Shoplifting Prevention 
Program and the Pointe Claire Youth 
Club. All of these programs have one 
point in common: visits are organized 
to reach the youth directly in their 
elementary or high-school environ- 
ments. 


It is difficult to evaluate with any real 
precision the impact that these four 
programs have had. However, on a 
quantitative level, we can say that 
over 3,000 students, from both the 
elementary and high-school levels, 
benefited from the judicious counsel 
of our youth workers. This is without 
a doubt an excellent average! 


International 
Development 


The Montreal YMCA is not content 
with its role of social entrepreneur 
here in Montreal. As a result, it also 
intervenes on an international level. 


During the past year, the YMCA 
International Development Depart- 
ment completed a strategic-planning 
study which resulted in the drafting 
of an new statement of principles 
and the drawing up of new goals and 
objectives. 


The Montreal YMCA believes that 
international development is a sector 
of intervention which requires that 
measures be taken both on a local 
and international level. On a local 
level, its interventions took the form 
of sensitization activities related to 
development. Also, the international 
programs department used other 
tools to continue this work, notably 
its newsletter, Qué Pasa. 


On the international scene, the 
Montreal YMCA, through its Saint- 
Laurent branch, formed a partnership 
with the Quito YMCA, in Ecuador. 
The daily reality experienced by the 
inhabitants of this country is typical of 
that endured by the people of Latin 
America in general. Close to 70% of 
the population is affected by acceler- 
ating impoverishment, as the gap 
between the poor and the rich con- 
stantly widens. As a next step, the 
Montreal YMCA and Quito YMCA will 
have to draft an agreement governing 
their partnership and take concrete 
action to help the residents of this 
city. 


Accessibility 


True to its role of social entrepreneur, 
the Montreal YMCA adopted a policy 
through which its centres are open to 
everyone, regardless of age, sex, 
religion, race or financial situation. 


During the course of the past year, 
given the economic situation in 
Montreal, the Association provided 
financial support to an increasing 
number of families and individuals 
who wanted to take advantage of its 
programs and services. Overall, the 
Montreal YMCA branches granted 
over 1,000 subsidies which were 
applicable to its memberships and 
programs. Moreover, the Hochelaga- 
Maisonneuve YMCA innovated in this 
area by agreeing to subsidize group 
memberships. 


All this, proves one thing: when the 
YMCA says that nobody will be 
refused access to its facilities and 
programs because of their inability 
to pay, it is not a case of empty 
promises! 


Conclusion 


Evidently, the programs and projects 
which have been mentioned in this 
report are only a small sample of all 
the community programming of the 
Montreal YMCA. Whether it be 
through its Young Mothers Group in 
Pointe-Saint-Charles, project at Place 
Benoit in Saint-Laurent, Youth Centre 
in Saint-Louis-du-Parc, or Integration 
Program on the West Island, more 
than ever before, the Montreal YMCA 
is fulfilling its role as SOCIAL 
ENTREPRENEUR. 


An everyday scene 
in the city of Quito, 
in Equador.

have been profitable.

Honorary Members and Governor 
In October 1990, the Foundation 
inducted Messrs. Roland Breton and 
David C. Roche as Honorary Members 
and Mr. André Chagnon as Governor 
of the Foundation. 


The Gabrielle and 

Maurice A. Massé Award 

In April 1991, the annual banquet of 
the Heritage Club was held. At this 
event, Mr. David M. Coyle received 
the Gabrielle and Maurice A. Massé 
award which is given to an individual 
who, over the years, has made a sig- 
nificant contribution to the Montreal 
YMCA. 


David M. Coyle sat on the Board of 
Directors of the Montreal YMCA as 
early as 1969. After having chaired 
several committees, he became 
Chairman of the Montreal YMCA in 
1978, at a time when the YMCA was 
going through an extremely difficult 
period in its history. It is thanks to 
David's cool-headedness and sense 
of professionalism and leadership 
that the Montreal YMCA was able to 
emerge a much stronger institution 
and continue to pursue its humanita- 
rian work. 


In August 1990, Mrs. Diane Tétreault 
joined the Foundation as its Director 
General. Her YMCA experience and 
knowledge of the Montreal community 
have been an invaluable asset to the 
Corporation. 


The Montreal YMCA Foundation 
continues to pursue its mandate of 
developing the financial resources of 
the Montreal YMCA with great 
confidence and enthusiasm. 


John E. ieee op 


Report of the 
President of the 
Montreal YMCA 
Foundation, 

Mr. Bernard W. Matte 


11 


Fiscal 1990-91 has been a year in 

which we consolidated all our financ- 
ing programs, given the difficult eco- 
nomic situation that we all experienced. 


Under the chairmanship of Mrs. 
Suzanne Aboud, our teams of 
volunteers and employees worked 
extremely hard during the annual 
Sustaining Membership Campaign. 
Close to 2,700 donors made generous 
contributions to the Campaign. 
Moreover, the team responsible for 
the Endowment and Planned Giving 
Program, under the leadership of Mr. 
Maurice A. Massé, helped secure the 
future of the Montreal YMCA. The 
overall endowment fund has a 
promissory value of $874,968 and 
the total bequests have a sound 
value of $752,490. To date, 25 indi- 
viduals have designated the Montreal 
YMCA as a beneficiary in their wills 
and 7 have purchased insurance 
policies naming the YMCA as sole 
beneficiary. It should be noted that 
over 155 people are members of the 
Gold Triangle and Heritage Clubs. 


YMCA Special Events have also 
helped finance the Montreal YMCA. 
Thanks to generous sponsors, the 
annual golf tournament, benefit 
evening and Y-A-Thon met their 
financial objectives. 


The Golf Tournament netted $35,000, 
which was transferred to our com- 
munity programs department which, 
in turn, committed this money to 
help young people who experience 
difficulty with the law and youth from 


fom 


visible minority groups who are 
looking for work. We wish to express 
our heartfelt thanks to our Patrons of 
Honor, namely the Royal Bank of 
Canada, Télé-Direct, Sun Life of 
Canada, Merck Frosst Canada Inc., 
Les Caisses populaires Desjardins, 
Bell Canada, Ultramar Canada Inc., 
Saint Lawrence Cement Inc., and 

17 other sponsors. 


The benefit evening was held on 
April 2, 1991 in théatre Port-Royal at 
Place des Arts. The performance of 
“Le Prix" by Arthur Miller helped raise 
$23,650 in ticket sales. We wish to 
express our sincere thanks to our 
partner-sponsors: Saint Lawrence 
Cement, Hydro-Québec and Samson, 
Bélair, Deloitte and Touche. 


The Y-A-Thon, which was held on 
November 18, 1990, generated profits 
totalling $80,000. Some 1,300 people, 
who succeeded in confirming 13,000 
sponsors, participated in the event. 
The Y-A-Thon was made possible 
through the contributions of the fol- 
lowing sponsors: Télé-Direct, Sun 
Life of Canada, Pratt & Whitney and 
Le Groupe CIG Inc. At this time, | 
wish to personally thank all the vol- 
unteers and employees who, once 
again this year, supported the 
Montreal YMCA and the Foundation. 


Bernard W. Matte
